title: Ride-sharing legalised; point-to-point transport reform (NSW)
summary: NSW put the first point-to-point reforms in place on 18 December 2015, allowing ride-sharing, then enacted the Point to Point Transport (Taxis and Hire Vehicles) Act 2016, whose main framework commenced 1 November 2017.

instruments.title: Point to Point Transport (Taxis and Hire Vehicles) Act 2016 No 34
Point to Point Transport (Taxis and Hire Vehicles) Act 2016 commencement proclamation
instruments.provisions: Commenced Parts 2-8 and related Schedules on 1 Nov 2017

commenced.what: First major point-to-point reforms in place (ride-sharing permitted under interim arrangements)
Main regulatory framework of the 2016 Act commenced

direction_rationale: Legalising app-based ride-share removes the legal barrier to entry created by taxi/hire-car licence quotas, adding a new type of supplier and price competition in point-to-point transport.
comparison: States that had not yet legalised ride-sharing (ACT Oct 2015 first, NT Dec 2017/Feb 2018 last)
confounders: taxi licence compensation and per-trip levies
ABN registration by gig drivers inflates business counts
